mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility has recovered to near-baseline (t-0w: +2.0%) after recent volatility, signaling normalization of essential-goods purchasing patterns. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below the prior 28-day mean, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts to negative territory in more than two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility has stabilized at -26.9% (t-0w), indicating a persistent floor in commuting demand. This sustained suppression of transit use reflects entrenched remote-work or avoidance behavior that will continue to depress retail-recreation visits concentrated in transit-adjacent zones over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has remained between -25.4% and -36.3% across all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -15% in any single week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite TRANSIT remaining below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has oscillated sharply (t-3w: -42.7%, t-1w: +9.9%, t-0w: -5.6%), indicating volatile outdoor-activity demand. When parks mobility is negative, consumers redirect discretionary time and spending toward indoor retail-recreation venues. The current negative parks reading (-5.6%) will sustain this redirection, lifting retail-recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility is negative in current week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above +5% in the first week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC declines in weeks 1–2 of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has remained consistently elevated (range: +2.0% to +7.0%), indicating sustained time-at-home behavior. High residential mobility combined with suppressed workplace mobility (t-0w: -15.7%) signals a shift toward home-based consumption and online retail, which will suppress in-person retail-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at t-0w is +3.9%, WORKPLACES at t-0w is -15.7%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next 28 days, or WORKPLACES rises above baseline while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

This partial recovery in workplace access will trigger a lagged recovery in retail-recreation visits as commuters resume weekday shopping routines over the next two weeks.

failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility falls below -20% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in week 2 of the forecast period.

This gap indicates that even workers returning to offices are avoiding public transit, likely using private transport or remaining remote. This transit avoidance will persist, keeping retail-recreation venues in transit-dependent zones suppressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -26.9%, WORKPLACES is -15.7%, gap of -11.2 points
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -15% while WORKPLACES remains below -10%, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite the transit-workplace gap persisting.

Concurrent with this reversal, retail-recreation is at -5.3%, near its recent low. The shift away from parks will redirect discretionary activity indoors, but only if residential time-at-home remains elevated (currently +3.9%). This interaction will suppress retail-recreation further over the next week as consumers substitute parks with home-based activities rather than retail.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at t-0w is -5.6%, RESIDENTIAL at t-0w is +3.9%
